result.summary:
Scope test: this diff adds a new schema-per-tenant table (event_type_registry) storing/validating arbitrary tenant-supplied JSON payloads and JSON Schema documents -- self-evidently a tenant-data path. Full review run against INV-1..INV-8. VERDICT: PASS, no invariant failed.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES. register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2 (registry.ex) each take tenant_id as an explicit, caller-supplied Ecto.UUID.t() -- last positional argument in every @spec. Every one of them resolves the physical schema via a private resolve_schema_name/1 (registry.ex, ~line 233-238): `Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id)` against Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Registration (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex, table tenant_schemas) -- a genuine DB lookup, not a header/payload/JWT-claim derivation, and this is byte-for-byte the same pattern already established and presumably-reviewed in TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 (tenant_provisioning.ex line 161). tenant_id is never read from attrs, the JSON payload, or the JSON Schema document -- EventType.changeset/2 (event_type.ex) only casts [:name, :schema_version, :json_schema, :description]; any tenant_id/prefix key present in attrs would be silently ignored by cast/4, not honored. Every DB call in registry.ex explicitly threads prefix: schema_name (get_type/2: `Repo.one(prefix: schema_name)`; insert_with_monotonicity_check/2: `Repo.one(prefix: schema_name)` for the max-version precheck and `Repo.insert(changeset, prefix: schema_name)` for the write) -- schema-per-tenant is genuinely enforced on every query, not partially. The migration (priv/repo/migrations/20260816163103_create_event_type_registry.exs) creates event_type_registry with `prefix: prefix()` under an `if prefix()` guard (no-ops on a plain `mix ecto.migrate`, matching REQ-022's established convention) and the EventType schema (event_type.ex) declares no static prefix -- it is resolved per-call only. The table has NO tenant_id column at all; tenant separation is purely physical-schema, so there is no shared-table-plus-forgotten-filter leak surface. tenant_scoped_migrations/0 (tenant_provisioning.ex) now includes {20_260_816_163_103, CreateEventTypeRegistry}, so replay_migrations/2 will actually provision this table per-tenant. PASS.

INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API/controller/response-serialization surface in this diff (S4 not started); registry.ex is a context module with no HTTP-facing caller yet (confirmed via grep -- zero call sites of Registry.register_type/validate_payload/get_type anywhere else in the repo).

INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. S5 not started; no Lua/WASM surface touched.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (live invariant). No secret material (API keys, tokens, DB URLs) appears anywhere in the 6 files reviewed. grep for System.get_env / hardcoded-secret heuristics against lib/letflow/event_store returned zero hits. This module has no config/env resolution surface at all. PASS (nothing to leak).

INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No multi-tenant lookup-by-ID HTTP endpoint exists yet (S4 not started); get_type/2 is an internal context function, not wired to any handler.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff itself: every new data-access path in the diff (register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2, the event_type_registry migration) has been explicitly checked against INV-1 above and shown to route through the schema-per-tenant mechanism.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES (live invariant). grep for `Repo.query`/`Repo.query!` across lib/letflow/event_store and priv/repo/migrations returned zero hits -- confirmed by direct read of registry.ex and json_schema.ex. All DB access goes through Ecto.Query composition (import Ecto.Query; where/order_by/limit/select) and Repo.one/2, Repo.insert/2, Repo.get_by/2 -- all parameterized by construction. The migration uses only the Ecto.Migration DSL (create table/create unique_index), no Ecto.Migration.execute/1 raw SQL. JsonSchema.validate/2 (json_schema.ex) is a pure, I/O-free recursive function over already-decoded Elixir maps -- it never touches Repo or builds any SQL string; the arbitrary tenant-supplied JSON Schema document and event payload only ever reach the database as an Elixir map cast into a jsonb-typed Ecto field (EventType.changeset/2's `cast(attrs, [..., :json_schema, ...])`), never as interpolated SQL text. PASS.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES (live invariant). grep heuristic `^\s*\{:ok, .*\} = ` hit one line (registry.ex ~line 248: `{:ok, %EventType{} = event_type} ->`) -- manually confirmed this is a `case` clause inside `case Repo.insert(changeset, prefix: schema_name) do ... end` with both {:ok, _} and {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} branches present, not a bare crashing match; false positive. Every I/O-touching path handles both outcomes explicitly: Jason.decode/1 in decode_object_payload/1 (registry.ex) matches {:ok, map}/{:ok, non-map}/{:error, _} all three; resolve_schema_name/1 case-matches nil/%Registration{}; get_type/2's Repo.one result is case-matched nil/%EventType{}; insert_with_monotonicity_check/2's Repo.insert result is case-matched {:ok,_}/{:error,%Ecto.Changeset{}} with a further unique_violation?/2 check mapping a race-lost unique-index hit to {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} rather than crashing. PASS.

:tenant_not_provisioned error path (rework iteration 1, acceptance criterion 3) -- specifically verified. resolve_schema_name/1's `Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id)` is an exact-match lookup scoped to the single tenant_id the caller passed -- it cannot return or iterate over any other tenant's row. On a miss it returns the bare atom {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} with no interpolated data (no schema_name, no other tenant's tenant_id, no count of provisioned tenants, no message string built from the lookup result) -- the atom carries zero information beyond 'this exact tenant_id has no Registration row'. No timing-based cross-tenant signal is introduced: the query is a single indexed exact-match lookup regardless of whether the tenant_id exists as some *other* tenant's row or no row at all. No leak.
